objective: Evaluate the effectiveness of the Nucleus-equipped mechanical heart valves in reducing thrombus formation rate compared to traditional mechanical heart valves.
independent_variables: Presence of Nucleus-equipped mechanical heart valves
dependent_variables: Thrombus formation rate on mechanical heart valves after 6 months of implantation
controls: Patient demographics, comorbidities, and medication regimens
baseline: Thrombus formation rate on traditional mechanical heart valves without the Nucleus
procedure: Recruit patients with aortic valve replacement surgery
Randomly assign patients to either the Nucleus-equipped mechanical heart valve group or the traditional mechanical heart valve group
Implant the assigned mechanical heart valves in the patients
Perform transesophageal echocardiography and histopathological analysis of explanted valves to measure thrombus formation rate
expected_result: A 40% reduction in thrombus formation rate on Nucleus-equipped mechanical heart valves compared to traditional mechanical heart valves after 6 months of implantation
falsification_condition: No significant reduction in thrombus formation rate on Nucleus-equipped mechanical heart valves compared to traditional mechanical heart valves after 6 months of implantation, as measured by transesophageal echocardiography and histopathological analysis of explanted valves
sample_requirements: A minimum of 100 patients per group, with a mix of age, sex, and comorbidities to ensure generalizability of the results
safety_constraints: Ensure that all patients are properly informed and consented for the study, and that the study is conducted in accordance with relevant regulations and guidelines
estimated_cost: $1 million (including personnel, equipment, and facility costs)
estimated_duration: 24 months (including recruitment, implantation, and follow-up periods)
information_gain: The results of this study will provide valuable insights into the effectiveness of the Nucleus-equipped mechanical heart valves in reducing thrombus formation rate, and will inform the development of future treatments for patients with mechanical heart valves
